context:
Goal: a session end cleans up after itself, and its cost can be stated.
Problem (rule): Your word on item 250 a (Nov 4, 07:00 CST) was "One repo at SessionEnd; machine-wide only in the daily job". The code does more: at session end it also stops dead servers anywhere on the machine. A fresh reviewer of PR #3238 found the two disagree. Only you can say which holds.
Based on (record): ruling watchers-sessionend-250a; decision the-janitor-is-one-machine-wide-sweep, section "Two triggers"; the header of janitor/session_end_sweep.py. Triage read all three.
Based on (your words): your note on 250 asked for parts of the daily job to run at session end too, because leftover processes stay too long. The "machine-wide" part in the janitor decision is the coordinator's reading, not your word. No later word of yours was found.
Based on (unmeasured): how many servers a session end stops, and what it costs.
Departs from: main — the hook stops dead servers on the whole machine at session end; a changes that to this repo only; b keeps main and records the machine-wide stop as your reading of your 250 note.
Meanwhile: the lane of #3238 writes both texts as they stand and keeps working. Nothing changes until you answer. The lane's second question (the mail doorbell) is not asked: ruling 3.15 already allows it, and the lane adds a pointer in hooks.md.
Reply 16:34 CST Nov 14 (to your save "this needs to be said simpler"): reworded in plain words. Same question, same two choices.
home: rulings watchers-sessionend-250a; decision the-janitor-is-one-machine-wide-sweep ("Two triggers"); janitor/session_end_sweep.py; steps watcher-builtin-hook-survey, watchers-plan-lanes

options.gain: One simple rule, as you picked: machine-wide work only in the daily job.
options.label: This repo only at session end. Dead servers elsewhere wait for the daily job. This is what your 250 a pick says.
options.lose: Leftover servers elsewhere stay until the daily job. A lane changes session_end_sweep.py and the janitor decision.

options.gain: Leftovers stop at once. No code change. The ruling text is rewritten to say so.
options.label: Keep the machine-wide stop of dead servers at session end, and record it as your reading of your 250 note (recommended: the code already does it, and your note asked for more at session end).
options.lose: A session end touches processes outside its own repo (dead ones only, so no live session's server). Its cost stays unmeasured until a cost pin measures it.
